item.title: High turnout as Israel goes to the polls in most consequential election in its history – live updates
item.description:
Will Bibi survive? Israelis head to the polls today for the first election since the October 7, 2023, attacks. The election is widely seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu's, or Bibi's, governance. Supporters say the last few years have been a success, as he "seized half of Gaza, dramatically expanded West Bank settlements, decimated Hezbollah in Lebanon and coaxed President Donald Trump into going to war against Iran," per The Washington Post —"all while offering a full-throated defense of Israel against accusations of war crimes and genocide." But "many of those who seek change have rallied around the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot, a centrist former military chief who, according to final polls this week, was running slightly ahead of Netanyahu," reports The Washington Post. item.description:
Having lost the first round of Brazil’s presidential election to far right rival Flávio Bolsonaro, incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva spectacularly triumphed in the second. What comes next for Brazil? The Guardian’s Tom Phillips is answering your questions now. Ask a question: log in or sign up here to comment, or email conversations@theguardian.com Jeremy Hurley asks: Why did the Brazil stock market tank after the election result, and will it recover? item.title: Trump administration asks Washington to set aside hundreds of ballots from suspected noncitizen voters
item.description:
Newsom accuses Trump of ‘assault on democracy’ as DoJ claims 20,000 registered voters in state are non-citizens A US federal appeals court rejected the Trump administration’s move to block California from counting the ballots of 20,000 registered voters that the justice department claims are non-citizens. The court on Monday ruled 2-1 against Donald ⁠Trump’s justice department in the dispute, denying the administration’s demand that election officials segregate the thousands of ballots until people on the list could verify their citizenship. The justice department had given the California secretary of state 48 hours to carry out the order, which state election officials refused – leading to the lawsuit. Continue reading...

item.title: Israelis are voting on whether to oust Netanyahu in first election since Oct. 7 attack
item.description:
Israelis cast ballots in a tight election with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fighting to retain power, but analysts cautioned the vote was unlikely to significantly alter the country’s stance on foreign policy or security. Israelis are divided on key issues, including threats to their country’s democratic institutions and settler violence, but “ the public is practically united on many security-related questions ,” The Wall Street Journal said. If anything, “ a shift in tone might be the biggest foreign policy change ,” experts at the Council on Foreign Relations noted. Still, the world’s attitude towards Israel may change depending on who holds power: The EU is more likely to impose long-threatened sanctions if the current national security minister remains in government, Rapporteur noted. — Prashant Rao

item.title: How ICE Operates in the Shadows
item.description:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents on March 24, 2026 in New York, New York. —Michael M. Santiago—Getty Images During the presidential election of 1863, at the height of the Civil War, federal troops reportedly descended on polling places in Delaware, Kentucky, Maryland, and Missouri and prevented people they deemed disloyal from voting. This prompted a fierce national debate that culminated in Congress passing an 1865 law barring federal “troops or armed men” from “any place” where an election is being held. The central goal of this law, according to its proponents, was “to prevent the President and his officers from interfering in elections,” which are run by the states. item.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
item.description:
Jordanian air force says it carried out strikes against ‘terrorist groups’ tied to killing of nine during funeral Jordan has carried out airstrikes against armed groups in Syria in retaliation for Friday’s attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the southern Jordanian governorate of Karak that killed nine people, the Jordanian air force has said in a statement. It said the operation “resulted in the killing and wounding of many members of these terrorist groups and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”. It did not specify who the groups were or the precise location of the strikes. Continue reading...

item.title: Brazil: defeated Flávio Bolsonaro ordered to surrender passports
item.description:
Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term as president, defeating the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in a dramatic comeback. Lula is the first candidate to win a runoff election after losing in the first round, taking victory with 51.79% of the vote to his rival’s 48.21%. His win bucks a regional trend, after the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro had spearheaded a radical populist movement. But with Flávio Bolsonaro refusing to concede defeat, what’s next for Brazil? Michael Safi speaks to Latin America correspondent Tom Phillips – watch on YouTube Continue reading...
